step1.text:
glim: searches X (Twitter) posts with advanced operators (from:, min_faves:, since:) and returns the matching posts with their engagement
Price: $0.005 per call, paid by this machine's wallet straight to the provider.
Request: POST https://glim.sh/api/v1/twitter/search
Inputs:
- query (string, required); X search terms, not a sentence: a few keywords plus operators such as from:handle, min_faves:N or since:YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. x402 from:coinbase min_faves:50. A sentence matches few or no posts. Put the sort in `sort`, not here. min_faves holds only with sort "latest": under "top", posts below it still...; min length 1; max length 1000
- cursor (string); Pagination cursor; max length 500
- expand_urls (boolean); When true, auto-crawl entity URLs and attach crawled_content to tweets. Off by default: responses can grow by up to 4KB per expanded URL. Use glim_web_crawl(url) for targeted crawls instead.; default false
- sort (string); Sort order: "top" (most engaged matching tweets) or "latest" (newest first). Default: "top".; one of "latest", "top"
Example input: {"query":"from:elonmusk AI min_faves:100"}
Example of what comes back (shortened): {"count":1,"has_more":true,"next_cursor":"abc123","tweets":[{"author":{"username":"elonmusk"},"id":"123","text":"Hello"}]}
To run it, call request({id: "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002", input: {...}}) with the inputs above. Nothing has been paid.

author.name: Digest D
author.description: A job board account that reposts hiring posts.

observed: 13 posts came back. 2 linked an employer board (Ashby, Greenhouse). Most others were digest or aggregator accounts that list many jobs in one post, several in other cities and fields, so review must judge fit per post. Post 4 is edited from a real post (its real one linked a third-party job site) to give a hiring post with no link, which is the lead case of ruling 16.
